theme: Autumn Sunday sauce week — one big rustic ragu and a jar of olive-oil beans carry four kid-friendly dinners for the full house.

components.name: Sunday ragu (pork + beef sugo)
components.ingredients: 1 lb ground pork, 1 lb ground beef (chuck), 2 onions, 2 carrots, 2 celery ribs, 4 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 cup dry white or red wine, two 28-oz cans whole peeled tomatoes (crushed by hand), 1 cup whole milk, bay, generous olive oil, salt
components.method: Build a slow soffritto: sweat finely diced onion, carrot and celery in a good pour of olive oil over low-medium heat until soft and sweet, 12-15 min, then add garlic. Push to the side, brown the pork and beef in batches so it caramelizes rather than steams. Stir in tomato paste and cook 2 min, deglaze with wine and reduce by half. Add the hand-crushed tomatoes and bay, bring to a bare simmer, then pour in the milk. Simmer uncovered 60-75 min until glossy and thick, stirring now and then. Cool and refrigerate; it only gets better by midweek and freezes beautifully.

components.name: Olive-oil braised cannellini beans (conserva)
components.ingredients: 1.5 lb dried cannellini (soaked overnight) or 4 cans drained, 1 head garlic halved crosswise, several sage leaves, 2 rosemary sprigs, 1 dried chili (optional), 1.5 cups olive oil, salt
components.method: Put drained soaked beans in a pot with the garlic, herbs, chili and enough water to cover by two inches. Add a big glug of olive oil and bring to the gentlest simmer; cook 60-75 min until creamy, salting generously in the last 15 min (canned beans: simmer 25 min in the oil, garlic and herbs instead). Let them cool in their liquid, then store beans plus the silky, herb-scented broth together. That broth is liquid gold for soups and for finishing greens.

dinners.name: Pappardelle al ragu
dinners.ingredients: Sunday ragu, 1.5 lb pappardelle or rigatoni, parmesan, butter, olive oil, reserved pasta water
steps: Warm a big ladle of ragu per person in a wide pan.
Boil pasta one minute shy of al dente, reserving a mug of starchy water.
Drag the pasta straight into the sauce with a splash of pasta water and a knob of butter.
Toss hard over the heat until the sauce clings and glosses (the mantecatura), loosening with more water as needed.
Finish off heat with grated parmesan and a thread of olive oil; serve with extra cheese for the girls.

dinners.name: Baked polenta with ragu & mozzarella
dinners.ingredients: 2 cups polenta, ragu, 2 balls mozzarella (torn), parmesan, butter, milk, olive oil
steps: Cook polenta in salted water (and a splash of milk) until creamy, finishing with butter and parmesan.
Spread half in a baking dish, spoon over ragu, scatter torn mozzarella.
Layer the rest of the polenta, more ragu and the remaining mozzarella.
Bake at 425F for 20-25 min until bubbling and browned at the edges.
Rest 5 min, drizzle with olive oil; a crowd-pleaser that reheats well for lunchboxes.

dinners.name: White bean & kale soup with garlic toast
dinners.ingredients: Bean conserva + its broth, 1 bunch lacinato kale, 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, parmesan rind, crusty bread, olive oil
steps: Soften chopped onion and garlic in olive oil; add a parmesan rind.
Add the beans with their broth plus water or stock to loosen; simmer 10 min.
Stir in shredded kale and cook until tender, 8-10 min; mash some beans against the pot to thicken.
Toast thick bread, rub with garlic, pour on olive oil; float a slice in each bowl.
Finish with grated parmesan and a heavy drizzle of olive oil (serve kids a brothier, milder bowl).

dinners.name: Seared cod over warm white beans & greens
dinners.ingredients: 2.5 lb cod or other mild white fish, bean conserva, 1 bunch spinach or chard, lemon, garlic, olive oil, parsley
steps: Pat fish very dry, salt, and sear in olive oil over medium-high until golden and just opaque, 3-4 min a side.
In another pan, warm beans in a little of their broth with garlic and olive oil.
Wilt the greens into the beans with a squeeze of lemon.
Spoon the beans and greens onto plates and set the fish on top.
Finish with lemon, parsley and olive oil; flake the kids' portions off the bone-free fillet into the beans.

technique.name: Mantecatura (emulsifying pasta off the heat)
technique.tiedTo: Pappardelle al ragu — pull the pasta early, toss it hard with starchy water, butter and cheese so the sauce emulsifies into a glossy coat that clings to every ribbon instead of pooling on the plate.

shopping.items: 2 onions, 1 extra onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery ribs, 1 head + 2 cloves garlic, 1 bunch lacinato kale, 1 bunch spinach or chard, 2 lemons, fresh sage, rosemary, parsley, bay
2.5 lb cod or other mild white fish fillets
1 lb ground pork, 1 lb ground beef chuck
2 balls fresh mozzarella, parmesan (plus a rind), whole milk, butter
1.5 lb dried cannellini (or 4 cans), two 28-oz cans whole peeled tomatoes, tomato paste, dry wine, 1.5 lb pappardelle or rigatoni, 2 cups polenta, crusty bread, dried chili, good olive oil, salt

scaleNote: Full-house week (6 at the table: you, Mike + the four girls). Quantities above are already set for 6, with leftovers by design — the ragu makes ~8-10 servings so you can freeze a batch, and the beans stretch across both the soup and the fish nights. Keep the kids' bowls brothier and milder: pull their soup before the garlic toast soaks in, grate extra parmesan on the pappardelle, and flake the cod into the beans so there's nothing to fuss over. If an evening gets hectic, the baked polenta is the make-ahead hero — assemble it in the afternoon and bake at dinnertime.
